_readme: Evidence for LTX-2.3 - the open-weight local video option that actually has weights.
It earns its place in this phase for two reasons beyond being open. First, it is the
honest answer to the local-video question that Wan 2.7 was expected to answer and
cannot (see wan.json). Second, it has a real legal-value GRID rather than a range,
and CineBraid's existing quantiser already expresses it - which is the useful kind of
proof that an architecture generalises: a second model needed no new mechanism.

license.name: ltx-2-community-license-agreement
license.note: NOT Apache. Its terms have not been read and must be before anything ships on it.

capabilities.claim: Joint audio-video generation in a single model.
Text-to-video and image-to-video pipelines are published.
Width and height must be divisible by 32.
Frame count must be divisible by 8 plus 1.
LoRA and IC-LoRA training are supported and reproducible.
LTX-2.3 improves audio and visual quality and prompt adherence over LTX-2.

notEstablished.status: not published on the model card
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: IMPORTANT. constraints.frameQuantiser carries fps 24 so the grid can be expressed and exercised at all, and the quantiser record says in its own note that the fps is CineBraid's assumption and must be confirmed before dispatch. This is the one place in the C2a catalogue where a number CineBraid supplied sits beside vendor facts, and it is labelled where a reader will see it.

notEstablished.status: not published; the repo states CUDA >12.7 and PyTorch ~=2.7 only
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: constraints.vramGuidanceGb is null. A 22B video model is not a laptop model, but CineBraid does not publish a number it cannot cite.
